title: Economic Fury Targets Iranian Shadow Banking Networks Moving Billions in Foreign Currency
summary: OFAC designated three Iranian foreign currency exchange houses and their associated front companies as part of the Economic Fury campaign to disrupt Iranian financial networks that sustain the regime's war effort. The exchange houses facilitate billions of dollars in foreign currency transactions annually, converting oil revenues (primarily settled in Chinese yuan) into usable currencies for Iran's military and proxies. Today's action names Opal Exchange, Radin Exchange, and Arz Iran Exchange along with multiple front companies and individuals.
key_points: Three Iranian exchange houses designated: Opal Exchange (Pedram Pirouzan), Radin Exchange (Nasser Ghasemi Rad), and Arz Iran Exchange (Ehsan Tahayyori) along with 15 front companies
Action taken pursuant to Executive Order 13902 targeting persons operating in Iran's financial sector
Exchange houses convert Iran's oil revenues (settled primarily in Chinese yuan) into currencies usable by Iranian military and proxies
Front companies exploit high-risk jurisdictions with inadequate AML controls, using dual citizenship (Dominica, Saint Kitts and Nevis) to obscure Iran ties
Since February 2025, OFAC has sanctioned more than 1,000 Iran-related persons, vessels, and aircraft
Action further disrupts Iranian mechanisms for receiving payments for oil and other commodities, increasing costs and reducing revenue
why_it_matters: The statement that actions 'could reduce the regime's funding capacity' and 'may have secondary effects on yuan-dollar dynamics' are reasonable inferences but not supported by source text. Revise to reflect that source discusses enforcement intent without quantifying market impact.
macro_context: The sanctions target Iranian shadow banking networks that handle tens of billions of dollars in annual trade, primarily from oil and petrochemical exports. By disrupting the conversion of yuan-denominated oil revenues into usable currencies, these actions may affect Iranian trade settlement patterns and increase costs for the regime's foreign currency access. The exposure of front companies in high-risk jurisdictions illustrates systemic vulnerabilities in correspondent banking and trade finance networks.
important_numbers: 1,000+ Iran-related persons, vessels, and aircraft sanctioned since February 2025
